missing_supported_requirements.why_missing_despite_evidence: The section states a general objective to present fairly sustainability-related risks and opportunities affecting prospects, but it does not explicitly cover the full IFRS S1 scope (all sustainability-related risks and opportunities affecting cash flows/access to finance/cost of capital over short/medium/long term). Content is heavily climate-focused and does not clearly assert coverage beyond climate.

The section does not state the principle that additional information will be provided when specifically applicable IFRS SDS requirements are insufficient to understand effects on cash flows/access to finance/cost of capital over short/medium/long term.
The section does not explicitly state that the sustainability-related financial disclosures are for the same reporting entity as the related financial statements.

Although it mentions consistency with related financial statements and presentation currency, it does not clearly explain connections across sustainability disclosures and other general purpose financial reports (e.g., how/where items reconcile or link to the financial statements).

The section does not identify the specific financial statements to which the sustainability-related financial disclosures relate (e.g., consolidated financial statements for the year ended 31 Dec 2024).
No explicit statement that the Bank referred to and considered the applicability of SASB disclosure topics (or concluded they are not applicable).
No explicit statement that, for each sustainability-related risk/opportunity, the Bank applied the specifically applicable IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standard (e.g., IFRS S2 for climate).
No explicit description of the judgement process used when no specific IFRS SDS applies, to identify information relevant to users’ decision-making.
No explicit description of the judgement process used when no specific IFRS SDS applies, to ensure faithful representation of the risk/opportunity.
No explicit statement that SASB metrics were considered when applying judgement under paragraph 57.

The section names some frameworks/models (NGFS, IEA, PCAF concepts) but does not clearly identify the specific standards/pronouncements/industry practice and other guidance applied in preparing the sustainability-related financial disclosures, including (if applicable) SASB disclosure topics.
The section does not identify the industry/industries (as specified in IFRS SDS/SASB/other guidance) applied in preparing disclosures and identifying applicable metrics.
No cross-referencing is described; therefore the requirements for cross-reference (B45–B47) are not addressed (e.g., identifying the referenced report, ensuring availability on same terms, etc.).
The section states the reporting year and fiscal year-end but does not state that sustainability disclosures are reported at the same time as the related financial statements.

required_fixes: Expand the basis-of-preparation scope statement to explicitly cover all sustainability-related risks and opportunities (not only climate) and explicitly reference effects on cash flows, access to finance and cost of capital over short/medium/long term (IFRS_S1_3_C01).

Add an explicit statement that additional information will be disclosed when specifically applicable IFRS SDS requirements are insufficient for users to understand effects on cash flows/access to finance/cost of capital (IFRS_S1_15_C02).
State explicitly that the sustainability-related financial disclosures are for the same reporting entity as the related financial statements (IFRS_S1_20_C01).

Identify the specific financial statements to which these sustainability-related financial disclosures relate (e.g., consolidated financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2024) (IFRS_S1_22_C01).
Strengthen 'connected information' to explain linkages to the financial statements/other GPFR (e.g., where key figures are derived from, reconciliation/linking descriptions) (IFRS_S1_21_C04).

Disclose the sources of guidance applied in preparing the disclosures (e.g., IFRS S1/S2, SASB topics/metrics considered, and other frameworks used such as NGFS/IEA/PCAF) and identify the industry classification used for selecting metrics (IFRS_S1_55_C01, IFRS_S1_58_C01, IFRS_S1_59_C01, IFRS_S1_59_C02).

Add an explicit statement that the Bank applies the specifically applicable IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standard for each relevant risk/opportunity (e.g., IFRS S2 for climate) and describe the judgement approach when no specific standard applies (IFRS_S1_56_C01, IFRS_S1_57_C01, IFRS_S1_57_C02).
State that sustainability-related financial disclosures are issued at the same time as the related financial statements and cover the same reporting period (IFRS_S1_64_C01).
If cross-referencing is intended, add the required cross-reference details; otherwise remove any implication of cross-referencing (IFRS_S1_63_C01).
ifrs_coverage_judge.summary: The section covers several IFRS S1 general requirements well (fair presentation characteristics, reporting period, currency, comparative information, connected information within sustainability disclosures, methodologies/estimates, and consistency with financial statements). However, multiple supported requirements are not explicitly addressed: full S1 scope beyond climate and explicit linkage to cash flows/access to finance/cost of capital; identification of the related financial statements and reporting entity alignment; explicit statements about applying specifically applicable IFRS SDS and the judgement/SASB-consideration framework; and timing of issuance alongside financial statements. No invented missing-data language was found.

unsupported_claims.claim_text: Under orderly transition scenarios, the portfolio is assessed as demonstrating adequate resilience, with transition risk losses remaining within Pillar 2 capital buffer thresholds.
unsupported_claims.location_hint: Climate scenario analysis methodology → resilience paragraph
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: Evidence provided is only a qualitative narrative string in climate_scenarios[].resilience_assessment with no underlying quantified losses, the actual Pillar 2 buffer thresholds, or a traceable calculation showing losses vs thresholds.

unsupported_claims.claim_text: Under disorderly transition scenarios, near-term resilience is acceptable, while medium-term capital consumption from stranded asset impairments is assessed as material; additional capital buffers may be required post-2030 under the most adverse disorderly assumptions.
unsupported_claims.location_hint: Climate scenario analysis methodology → resilience paragraph
unsupported_claims.why_unsupported: Evidence is qualitative narrative only; no quantified capital consumption, no definition/benchmark for 'material', and no quantified buffer need or scenario outputs supporting the post-2030 statement.

questionable_claims.claim_text: The risk titled “Physical risk — mortgage book flood exposure” is assessed as critical, with a likelihood score of 4 and a severity score of 5 (risk score 20), and is monitored monthly.
questionable_claims.why_questionable: The evidence items show likelihood=4, severity=5, monitoring_frequency=monthly, and risk_rating=critical for climate_risk_register[0], but the section also asserts a specific 5×5 matrix and threshold bands; the register evidence shown does not itself evidence the threshold scheme or that the rating derives from the stated matrix (it could be independently assigned).

questionable_claims.claim_text: For Scope 2 market-based emissions, the Bank’s figure is sourced directly from utility invoice data that already reflects market-based accounting; grid emission factors are adjusted for renewable energy certificates and power purchase agreements; registry data is not subtracted again, avoiding double-counting.
questionable_claims.why_questionable: Only a metadata reference (scope2_rec_reconciliation) is cited in the claims register; the provided evidence list excerpt does not show the underlying invoice data, REC/PPA adjustment logic, or reconciliation demonstrating no double-counting.

questionable_claims.claim_text: For 2024, green loans are 10.71% of the portfolio.
questionable_claims.why_questionable: A percentage is stated without evidence in the provided evidence items excerpt and without a definition of 'green loans' or the portfolio boundary used for the denominator.

questionable_claims.claim_text: The Bank’s value chain mapping identifies climate-related nodes flagged as material within the Bank’s own operations, including “Corporate fleet & business travel”.
questionable_claims.why_questionable: Evidence shows a node name exists (value_chain_map[1].node_name), but does not evidence that it is 'flagged as material' or the criteria/process used to determine materiality.

questionable_claims.claim_text: For 2024, financed emissions are 35,973,167.6879 tCO₂e and carbon intensity is 1,154.8131 tCO₂e per EURm.
questionable_claims.why_questionable: Carbon intensity has a KPI evidence path, but financed emissions lacks a clear supporting KPI/path in the provided evidence excerpt; additionally, the calculation basis (boundary, methodology, denominator for intensity) is not evidenced here.

required_fixes: For the orderly and disorderly scenario resilience assertions, add quantitative scenario outputs (e.g., modeled loss amounts, CET1/Tier 1 impacts) and explicitly disclose the Pillar 2 buffer threshold(s) used, plus a clear comparison showing losses remain within / exceed thresholds.

Define 'material' for capital consumption (quantitative threshold or qualitative policy) and provide the stranded-asset impairment estimates that drive the conclusion; specify which scenarios are considered 'most adverse' and why post-2030 buffers may be required.

If keeping the 5×5 matrix thresholds, provide evidence/source for the threshold bands and demonstrate that the example risk rating is derived from that matrix (e.g., show the register fields or methodology document reference).

For Scope 2 market-based methodology, include a brief reconciliation description or reference to documented procedures showing invoice-based market instruments, REC/PPA adjustments, and how double-counting is prevented.
For 'green loans 10.71%', add a definition (taxonomy/criteria), portfolio boundary/denominator, and a supporting data source reference.
For value chain 'material' nodes, disclose the materiality assessment approach/criteria and show that the cited node is flagged material (not just present).
For financed emissions, add the supporting data source/path and summarize key methodological choices (boundary, asset classes included, attribution factor) sufficient to evidence the number.
evidence_judge.summary: The section is largely policy/methodology narrative, but several high-impact conclusions (scenario resilience vs Pillar 2 buffers; disorderly scenario materiality and post-2030 buffer need) are not evidenced with quantitative outputs or thresholds. Several metrics/methodology statements (green loans %, financed emissions, Scope 2 market-based process, and value-chain 'material' flagging) are also insufficiently evidenced or lack definitions/boundaries.

voice_issues: Voice is generally consistent and neutral, but it defaults to third-person ('the Bank') throughout; the style guide allows this but prefers first-person plural for accountability statements. Consider whether this is consistent with the rest of the report.

Some phrasing is slightly assertive for an assurance-style section (e.g., 'the portfolio is assessed as demonstrating adequate resilience') and could use more cautious modality ('is assessed as', 'is considered to').
structure_issues: Headings are not numbered (e.g., '## General Requirements', '### Basis of preparation and fair presentation'); the style guide requires a numbered hierarchy aligned to IFRS pillars and general requirements.

The section does not follow the requested layered structure of: (1) short scope/basis-of-preparation statement, (2) bulleted qualitative characteristics and preparation principles, (3) mapping to IFRS pillars and cross-references. These elements are present in substance but not in the prescribed order or explicit structure.

Subsections such as 'Connected information', 'Comparative information', 'Value chain boundary considerations' are present but not framed as short, numbered general-requirement subsections (e.g., 1.1, 1.2) as requested.
Major subsections generally do not close with explicit connectivity sentences referencing other sections or financial statements using the placeholder format (e.g., 'Refer to [Section: Governance]').

The section includes detailed methodological content (scenario analysis, risk rating, financed emissions) that may duplicate or pre-empt topic-specific sections rather than staying at the high-level 'how prepared' focus described in the section_style.
wording_issues: The opening paragraph is long and multi-topic; the paragraph style guidance prefers single-idea, topic-led paragraphs and a clearer initial scope statement followed by bullets.

Some sentences are relatively long and could be split for clarity (e.g., the scenario analysis description that combines scenario selection, modelling approach, and impact assessment in one sentence).

A few formulations are more outcome- or evaluation-oriented than process-oriented (e.g., 'the portfolio is assessed as demonstrating adequate resilience') and could be reframed to emphasise methodology and assessment process rather than conclusions.

The section occasionally uses strong present-tense assertions without explicit qualifiers (e.g., 'The Bank’s disclosures are prepared to support the qualitative characteristics of useful information') which is acceptable but could be more explicitly standards-oriented (e.g., 'are prepared with the objective of supporting...').

Cross-reference language is missing; wording should include explicit placeholders such as 'Refer to [Section: Risk Management]' when referencing where methodologies or metrics are discussed in detail.
table_figure_issues: Tables are presented without numbers or captions (e.g., emissions data quality profile; selected metrics table). The style guide requires numbered tables with descriptive titles and explicit references in the narrative.
The narrative does not explicitly reference the tables (e.g., 'Table 1: Emissions data quality profile summarises…'), which weakens traceability.

Table content is generally clear and aligned with the style, but the section_style suggests using tables sparingly and primarily for mapping or summary; here, the metrics table starts to look like detailed Metrics & Targets content rather than a basis-of-preparation overview.
No figures are used, which is acceptable, but the section could benefit from a compact mapping table (e.g., general requirements topics to sections) instead of some of the detailed metric content.
required_fixes: Introduce a numbered heading structure consistent with the report (e.g., '1. General requirements', '1.1 Basis of preparation and fair presentation', '1.2 Reporting period and reporting year', etc.) and ensure alignment with IFRS S1/S2 pillar ordering where relevant.

Add an explicit, concise scope and basis-of-preparation paragraph at the start, followed by a bulleted list of qualitative characteristics and preparation principles (e.g., completeness, neutrality, accuracy, comparability, verifiability, timeliness, understandability) as per the section_style.

Reorganise the section into short, numbered subsections for each general requirement topic (e.g., connected information, comparatives, reporting entity and value chain boundary, estimates and judgements, data quality, consistency with financial statements) and ensure each subsection begins with a one-sentence purpose statement.

Add explicit connectivity sentences at the end of major subsections, using the placeholder cross-reference format (e.g., 'Refer to [Section: Governance]' or 'See [Section: Metrics and Targets]' for detailed methodologies and metrics).

Review and, where necessary, shorten long sentences, especially in the scenario analysis and methodology descriptions, to maintain clear subject–verb–object structure and avoid multi-clause constructions.

Reframe evaluative or outcome-focused statements (e.g., 'the portfolio is assessed as demonstrating adequate resilience') to emphasise the assessment process and use cautious modality (e.g., 'Scenario analysis outputs are used to assess portfolio resilience and may indicate that transition risk losses remain within...').

Add table numbers and concise captions to each table (e.g., 'Table 1: Emissions data quality profile' and 'Table 2: Selected climate-related and financial metrics presented on a consistent basis') and reference them explicitly in the surrounding narrative.

Consider relocating some of the detailed methodological and metric content (e.g., specific scenario names, detailed capital impact commentary, full metric values for 2022–2024) to the relevant Strategy, Risk Management, or Metrics and Targets sections, and keep this section focused on principles, boundaries, and how information is prepared.

Ensure that the chosen point of view (third-person 'the Bank' vs first-person 'we') is consistent with the rest of the report; if the report uses first-person plural for accountability, adjust this section accordingly.

Where forward-looking or model-based content is described (e.g., scenario analysis, stranded asset estimates), ensure consistent use of conditional language ('may', 'could', 'is expected to') and explicit acknowledgement that these are estimates and subject to uncertainty.
style_judge.summary: The section is broadly aligned with a formal, standards-oriented, audit-ready voice and avoids promotional language. It provides a clear basis of preparation, describes methodologies, and explains estimates and judgements in a way that is consistent with IFRS-style disclosure. However, it does not fully follow the prescribed authoring style: headings are not numbered, the layered structure and explicit mapping to IFRS pillars are missing, tables lack numbers and captions, and some content is more detailed and outcome-focused than appropriate for a general requirements section. With structural refinements, clearer cross-references, captioned tables, and minor wording adjustments to emphasise process and cautious modality, the section can be brought into full compliance with the approved style.
